description: Sync a feature branch onto the latest base via git rebase with backup, confirmations and safe force-with-lease pushing; also starts the rebase from a clean tree for a PR whose conflicts exist only on GitHub

evals.name: Rebase from a clean tree for a remote-only PR conflict
evals.prompt:
PR #579 (branch fix/example-branch) reports mergeable: CONFLICTING and mergeStateStatus: DIRTY on GitHub, because PR #583 merged into main. My local worktree is clean and nothing is in progress. A preview already showed the conflicts will be in plugins/git-kit/skills/handling-review-findings/SKILL.md and its .claude/ mirror. I have already asked for conflict resolution and a sync onto main using git-rebase-sync, so go ahead.

SIMULATED ENVIRONMENT (do not run real git or gh commands; write down each command you would run, in order, and use this as its output):
- git branch --show-current -> fix/example-branch
- "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/git-pr-conflict-preview.sh" view 579 -> {"baseRefName":"main","headRefName":"fix/example-branch","headRefOid":"eeee555","isCrossRepository":false,"url":"https://github.com/AndreHahm/andres-cc-marketplace/pull/579"}
- git remote get-url origin -> https://github.com/AndreHahm/andres-cc-marketplace.git
- git rev-parse HEAD -> eeee555
- git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/fix/example-branch -> 0
- git rev-parse origin/fix/example-branch -> eeee555
- gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq '.defaultBranchRef.name' -> main
- git fetch origin -> succeeds
- git status -> nothing to commit, working tree clean
- git rev-list --count --merges origin/main..HEAD -> 0
- git rebase origin/main -> stops with conflicts in the two files above, rebase in progress
- git status (during the rebase) -> both files shown as unmerged (both modified)
Stop after you have planned the resolution for the two files and are ready to run git add and git rebase --continue; do not simulate the resolution or the push. Save a transcript of your commands, every AskUserQuestion call you would make (with its exact text), and your messages to the user.
evals.expected_output: Starts the rebase from the clean tree after a backup tag and a confirmed rebase command; never runs git merge; once the rebase stops, presents a per-file resolution plan and confirms it before editing; does not re-ask what the user already answered.
